sanskrit: asyās tu pārśve kanakottamābhā; yaiṣā prabhā mūrtimatīva gaurī madhye sthitaiṣā bhaginī dvijāgryā; cakrāyudhasyāpratimasya tasya
english: At her side, with the radiance of finest gold—this fair one, a splendor as if made flesh—stands in the midst, O foremost of the twice-born, the sister of him whose weapon is the discus, that peerless one.

sanskrit: iyaṃ svasā rājacamūpates tu; pravṛddhanīlotpaladāmavarṇā paspardha kṛṣṇena nṛpaḥ sadā yo; vṛkodarasyaiṣa parigraho 'gryaḥ
english: This one, the sister of the lord of the royal host, of the hue of a thick garland of blue lotuses—she is the chief consort of Vṛkodara, the king who ever vied with Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca rājño magadhādhipasya; sutā jarāsaṃdha iti śrutasya yavīyaso mādravatīsutasya; bhāryā matā campakadāmagaurī
english: And this one, the daughter of the king who ruled Magadha, he famed as Jarāsaṃdha, fair as a garland of campaka blossoms, is held to be the wife of the younger son of Mādravatī.

sanskrit: indīvaraśyāmatanuḥ sthitā tu; yaiṣāparāsannamahītale ca bhāryā matā mādravatīsutasya; jyeṣṭhasya seyaṃ kamalāyatākṣī
english: And she who stands here, dark of body as a blue water-lily, seated upon the ground close by—this lotus-eyed one is held to be the wife of the elder son of Mādravatī.

sanskrit: iyaṃ tu niṣṭaptasuvarṇagaurī; rājño virāṭasya sutā saputrā bhāryābhimanyor nihato raṇe yo; droṇādibhis tair viratho rathasthaiḥ
english: And this one, golden-fair as refined gold, the daughter of King Virāṭa, here with her son—she was the wife of Abhimanyu, who was slain in battle, stripped of his chariot, by Droṇa and the rest who kept to their cars.

sanskrit: etās tu sīmantaśiroruhā yāḥ; śuklottarīyā nararājapatnyaḥ rājño 'sya vṛddhasya paraṃśatākhyāḥ; snuṣā vivīrā hataputranāthāḥ
english: And these women, their hair parted at the crown, clad in white upper garments, wives of warrior-kings—they are the more than a hundred daughters-in-law of this aged king, bereft of their heroes, their sons and lords slain.

sanskrit: etā yathāmukhyam udāhṛtā vo; brāhmaṇyabhāvād ṛjubuddhisattvāḥ sarvā bhavadbhiḥ paripṛcchyamānā; narendrapatnyaḥ suviśuddhasattvāḥ
english: These I have named to you in order of rank, O you of brahminic temper, upright in mind and being—all the wives of kings, of perfectly pure nature, of whom you have been inquiring.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa rājā kuruvṛddhavaryaḥ; samāgatas tair naradevaputraiḥ papraccha sarvān kuśalaṃ tadānīṃ; gateṣu sarveṣv atha tāpaseṣu
english: Thus that king, foremost of the Kuru elders, having met with those sons of kings, then inquired after the welfare of them all, once all the ascetics had departed.

sanskrit: yodheṣu cāpy āśramamaṇḍalaṃ taṃ; muktvā niviṣṭeṣu vimucya patram strīvṛddhabāle ca susaṃniviṣṭe; yathārhataḥ kuśalaṃ paryapṛcchat
english: And when the warriors too, leaving that ring of hermitages, had settled and laid aside their gear, and the women, the aged, and the children were comfortably seated, he asked after the welfare of each as was fitting.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho kaccit tāta kuśaly asi sahito bhrātṛbhiḥ sarvaiḥ paurajānapadais tathā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Yudhiṣṭhira, mighty-armed, is it well with you, my son, together with all your brothers and with the townsfolk and country-folk alike?

sanskrit: ye ca tvām upajīvanti kaccit te 'pi nirāmayāḥ sacivā bhṛtyavargāś ca guravaś caiva te vibho
english: And those who depend upon you—are they too free from ailment: your counsellors, the host of your servants, and your elders, O lord?

sanskrit: kaccid vartasi paurāṇīṃ vṛttiṃ rājarṣisevitām kaccid dāyān anucchidya kośas te 'bhiprapūryate
english: Do you follow the ancient way of life, that which the royal sages observed? Is your treasury filled without cutting off the rightful shares of others?

sanskrit: arimadhyasthamitreṣu vartase cānurūpataḥ brāhmaṇān agrahārair vā yathāvad anupaśyasi
english: Do you bear yourself fittingly toward foes, the neutral, and friends? And do you duly look after the brahmins with grants of land?

sanskrit: kaccit te parituṣyanti śīlena bharatarṣabha śatravo guravaḥ paurā bhṛtyā vā svajano 'pi vā
english: Are they content with your conduct, O bull of the Bhāratas—your enemies, your elders, the townsfolk, your servants, and your own kin as well?

sanskrit: kaccid yajasi rājendra śraddhāvān pitṛdevatāḥ atithīṃś cānnapānena kaccid arcasi bhārata
english: Do you, full of faith, worship the ancestors and the gods with sacrifice, O lord of kings, and honor guests with food and drink, O Bhārata?

sanskrit: kaccic ca viṣaye viprāḥ svakarmaniratās tava kṣatriyā vaiśyavargā vā śūdrā vāpi kuṭumbinaḥ
english: And in your realm, are the brahmins devoted to their own duties, and the kṣatriyas, the body of vaiśyas, and the householder śūdras as well?

sanskrit: kaccit strībālavṛddhaṃ te na śocati na yācate jāmayaḥ pūjitāḥ kaccit tava gehe nararṣabha
english: Do the women, children, and aged in your land neither grieve nor beg? Are the women of your house honored, O bull among men?

sanskrit: kaccid rājarṣivaṃśo 'yaṃ tvām āsādya mahīpatim yathocitaṃ mahārāja yaśasā nāvasīdati
english: Does this lineage of royal sages, having gained you as its lord of the earth, not sink in renown below what befits it, O great king?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity evaṃvādinaṃ taṃ sa nyāyavit pratyabhāṣata kuśalapraśnasaṃyuktaṃ kuśalo vākyakarmaṇi
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To him who spoke thus, asking after his welfare, that knower of right replied, himself skilled in the conduct of speech.

sanskrit: kaccit te vardhate rājaṃs tapo mandaśramasya te api me jananī ceyaṃ śuśrūṣur vigataklamā apy asyāḥ saphalo rājan vanavāso bhaviṣyati
english: Does your austerity prosper, O king, while your toil is light? And this mother of mine, who serves you—is she free from weariness? Will her dwelling in the forest, O king, bear its fruit?

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca mātā jyeṣṭhā me vītavātādhvakarśitā ghoreṇa tapasā yuktā devī kaccin na śocati
english: And this eldest mother of mine, worn by the buffeting of wind and journeys, the queen given to grim austerities—does she not grieve?

sanskrit: hatān putrān mahāvīryān kṣatradharmaparāyaṇān nāpadhyāyati vā kaccid asmān pāpakṛtaḥ sadā
english: Her sons of great valor, devoted to the kṣatriya code, are slain—does she not ever brood ill upon us as evildoers?

sanskrit: kva cāsau viduro rājan nainaṃ paśyāmahe vayam saṃjayaḥ kuśalī cāyaṃ kaccin nu tapasi sthitaḥ
english: And where is that Vidura, O king? We do not see him. And is this Saṃjaya well? Does he abide in austerity?

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro janādhipam kuśalī viduraḥ putra tapo ghoraṃ samāsthitaḥ
english: Thus addressed, Dhṛtarāṣṭra answered the lord of men: Vidura is well, my son; he has taken up a grim austerity.

sanskrit: vāyubhakṣo nirāhāraḥ kṛśo dhamanisaṃtataḥ kadā cid dṛśyate vipraiḥ śūnye 'smin kānane kva cit
english: Feeding on air, taking no food, gaunt, his veins standing out, he is now and then glimpsed by brahmins somewhere in this empty forest.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vadatas tasya jaṭī vīṭāmukhaḥ kṛśaḥ digvāsā maladigdhāṅgo vanareṇusamukṣitaḥ
english: Even as he was speaking thus, there appeared one with matted locks, a pebble in his mouth, emaciated, clad only in the directions, his limbs smeared with grime and sprinkled with the dust of the forest.

sanskrit: dūrād ālakṣitaḥ kṣattā tatrākhyāto mahīpateḥ nivartamānaḥ sahasā janaṃ dṛṣṭvāśramaṃ prati
english: From afar the Steward was spied and pointed out to the king there; but, seeing the company, he at once turned back toward the hermitage.

sanskrit: tam anvadhāvan nṛpatir eka eva yudhiṣṭhiraḥ praviśantaṃ vanaṃ ghoraṃ lakṣyālakṣyaṃ kva cit kva cit
english: After him ran the king, Yudhiṣṭhira, alone, as he entered the dread forest—now seen, now lost to view, here and there.

sanskrit: bho bho vidura rājāhaṃ dayitas te yudhiṣṭhiraḥ iti bruvan narapatis taṃ yatnād abhyadhāvata
english: "Ho, Vidura! I am the king, your beloved Yudhiṣṭhira!"—so crying, the lord of men pursued him with all his effort.

sanskrit: tato vivikta ekānte tasthau buddhimatāṃ varaḥ viduro vṛkṣam āśritya kaṃ cit tatra vanāntare
english: Then in a lonely, secluded spot the foremost of the wise, Vidura, came to a halt, leaning against a certain tree there in the depths of the wood.

sanskrit: taṃ rājā kṣīṇabhūyiṣṭham ākṛtīmātrasūcitam abhijajñe mahābuddhiṃ mahābuddhir yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: That man, all but wasted away, betrayed by his form alone, the keenly wise Yudhiṣṭhira recognized as the man of mighty understanding.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro 'ham asmīti vākyam uktvāgrataḥ sthitaḥ vidurasyāśrave rājā sa ca pratyāha saṃjñayā
english: "I am Yudhiṣṭhira," he said, and stood before him, within Vidura's hearing; and the other answered him by a sign.

sanskrit: tataḥ so 'nimiṣo bhūtvā rājānaṃ samudaikṣata saṃyojya viduras tasmin dṛṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭyā samāhitaḥ
english: Then, growing unblinking, Vidura gazed upon the king, fixing his sight upon him, wholly composed, eye joined with eye.

sanskrit: viveśa viduro dhīmān gātrair gātrāṇi caiva ha prāṇān prāṇeṣu ca dadhad indriyāṇīndriyeṣu ca
english: The wise Vidura entered into him, limb by limb into limbs, setting his vital breaths within his breaths and his senses within his senses.

sanskrit: sa yogabalam āsthāya viveśa nṛpates tanum viduro dharmarājasya tejasā prajvalann iva
english: Having recourse to the power of yoga, Vidura entered the body of the king, into the Dharma King, blazing as it were with splendor.

sanskrit: vidurasya śarīraṃ tat tathaiva stabdhalocanam vṛkṣāśritaṃ tadā rājā dadarśa gatacetanam
english: Vidura's body, just so, with its eyes fixed motionless, leaning against the tree and now bereft of consciousness, the king then beheld.

sanskrit: balavantaṃ tathātmānaṃ mene bahuguṇaṃ tadā dharmarājo mahātejās tac ca sasmāra pāṇḍavaḥ
english: And the Dharma King of great splendor then felt himself grown strong and enriched manifold; and the Pāṇḍava called that to mind.

sanskrit: paurāṇam ātmanaḥ sarvaṃ vidyāvān sa viśāṃ pate yogadharmaṃ mahātejā vyāsena kathitaṃ yathā
english: Learned, of great splendor, he recalled all his own ancient nature, O lord of peoples, and the law of yoga as it had been told by Vyāsa.

sanskrit: dharmarājas tu tatrainaṃ saṃcaskārayiṣus tadā dagdhukāmo 'bhavad vidvān atha vai vāg abhāṣata
english: Then the Dharma King, wishing to perform the last rites for him there, the learned one, desired to cremate him; but thereupon a voice spoke.

sanskrit: bho bho rājan na dagdhavyam etad vidurasaṃjñakam kalevaram ihaitat te dharma eṣa sanātanaḥ
english: "Ho, O king! This body, known by the name of Vidura, must not be burned. This is the eternal law for you here.

sanskrit: lokāḥ saṃtānakā nāma bhaviṣyanty asya pārthiva yatidharmam avāpto 'sau naiva śocyaḥ paraṃtapa
english: The worlds called Saṃtānaka shall be his, O prince; he has attained the law of the ascetic and is in no way to be mourned, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: ity ukto dharmarājaḥ sa vinivṛtya tataḥ punaḥ rājño vaicitravīryasya tat sarvaṃ pratyavedayat
english: So addressed, the Dharma King turned back from there once more and reported all of this to the son of Vicitravīrya.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā dyutimān sa ca sarvo janas tadā bhīmasenādayaś caiva paraṃ vismayam āgatāḥ
english: Then that splendid king, and all that company, and Bhīmasena and the rest as well, were filled with the greatest wonder.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā prītimān rājā bhūtvā dharmajam abravīt āpo mūlaṃ phalaṃ caiva mamedaṃ pratigṛhyatām
english: Hearing this, the king was glad, and said to the son of Dharma: "Let this water, these roots and fruit of mine be accepted."

sanskrit: yadanno hi naro rājaṃs tadanno 'syātithiḥ smṛtaḥ ity uktaḥ sa tathety eva prāha dharmātmajo nṛpam phalaṃ mūlaṃ ca bubhuje rājñā dattaṃ sahānujaḥ
english: "For whatever food a man eats, O king, of that same food his guest is held to partake." Thus addressed, the son of Dharma said only "So be it" to the king, and ate the fruit and roots given by him, together with his younger brothers.

sanskrit: tatas te vṛkṣamūleṣu kṛtavāsaparigrahāḥ tāṃ rātriṃ nyavasan sarve phalamūlajalāśanāḥ
english: Then they all, taking up their lodging at the roots of the trees, passed that night living on fruit, roots, and water.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ sā rajanī teṣām āśrame puṇyakarmaṇām śivā nakṣatrasaṃpannā sā vyatīyāya bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus that night of theirs, men of holy deeds, in the hermitage—auspicious and graced with stars—passed away, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatra tatra kathāś cāsaṃs teṣāṃ dharmārthalakṣaṇāḥ vicitrapadasaṃcārā nānāśrutibhir anvitāḥ
english: Here and there were their discourses, marked by dharma and artha, ranging through manifold turns of phrase, furnished with various sacred lore.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tv abhito mātur dharaṇyāṃ suṣupus tadā utsṛjya sumahārhāṇi śayanāni narādhipa
english: But the Pāṇḍavas slept that night on the bare ground all about their mother, having forsaken their most costly couches, O lord of men.

sanskrit: yadāhāro 'bhavad rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro mahāmanāḥ tadāhārā nṛvīrās te nyavasaṃs tāṃ niśāṃ tadā
english: On whatever fare the high-minded king Dhṛtarāṣṭra subsisted, on that same fare those heroes of men lived through that night.

sanskrit: vyatītāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ kṛtapūrvāhṇikakriyaḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha kaunteyo dadarśāśramamaṇḍalam
english: When the night had passed, the son of Kuntī, his early-morning rites performed, beheld together with his brothers the ring of hermitages.

sanskrit: sāntaḥpuraparīvāraḥ sabhṛtyaḥ sapurohitaḥ yathāsukhaṃ yathoddeśaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrābhyanujñayā
english: With the women of the household and his retinue, with his servants and his priest, he roamed at ease and at will, by Dhṛtarāṣṭra's leave.

sanskrit: dadarśa tatra vedīś ca saṃprajvalitapāvakāḥ kṛtābhiṣekair munibhir hutāgnibhir upasthitāḥ
english: There he saw the altars with their fires brightly ablaze, attended by sages who had bathed and made their offerings into the flames.

sanskrit: vāneyapuṣpanikarair ājyadhūmodgamair api brāhmeṇa vapuṣā yuktā yuktā munigaṇaiś ca tāḥ
english: With heaps of forest flowers and with the rising smoke of clarified butter, endowed with a holy aspect and thronged with bands of sages were those altars.

sanskrit: mṛgayūthair anudvignais tatra tatra samāśritaiḥ aśaṅkitaiḥ pakṣigaṇaiḥ pragītair iva ca prabho
english: With herds of deer, unstartled, sheltering here and there, and with flocks of birds, all unafraid and as if breaking into song, O lord—

sanskrit: kekābhir nīlakaṇṭhānāṃ dātyūhānāṃ ca kūjitaiḥ kokilānāṃ ca kuharaiḥ śubhaiḥ śrutimanoharaiḥ
english: with the cries of blue-throated peacocks, the calling of the gallinules, and the auspicious warbling of cuckoos, lovely to the ear—

sanskrit: prādhītadvijaghoṣaiś ca kva cit kva cid alaṃkṛtam phalamūlasamudvāhair mahadbhiś copaśobhitam
english: and adorned here and there with the sound of brahmins reciting their lessons, and graced with great burdens of fruit and roots borne along.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā pradadau tāpasārtham upāhṛtān kalaśān kāñcanān rājaṃs tathaivaudumbarān api
english: Then that king bestowed, for the ascetics' sake, the pots that had been brought—golden ones, O king, and likewise those of udumbara wood—

sanskrit: ajināni praveṇīś ca sruksruvaṃ ca mahīpatiḥ kamaṇḍalūṃs tathā sthālīḥ piṭharāṇi ca bhārata
english: and deerskins and woven mats, the sacrificial ladle and spoon, the water-jars, the cooking-pots and pans, O Bhārata—the lord of earth gave all these.

sanskrit: bhājanāni ca lauhāni pātrīś ca vividhā nṛpa yad yad icchati yāvac ca yad anyad api kāṅkṣitam
english: and iron vessels and dishes of many kinds, O king—whatever each one wished for, and however much, and whatever else was desired.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa rājā dharmātmā parītyāśramamaṇḍalam vasu viśrāṇya tat sarvaṃ punar āyān mahīpatiḥ
english: Thus that righteous king, having gone round the ring of hermitages and distributed all that wealth, the lord of earth returned again.

sanskrit: kṛtāhnikaṃ ca rājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ manīṣiṇam dadarśāsīnam avyagraṃ gāndhārīsahitaṃ tadā
english: And he beheld the wise king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, his daily rites performed, seated calm and untroubled together with Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: mātaraṃ cāvidūrasthāṃ śiṣyavat praṇatāṃ sthitām kuntīṃ dadarśa dharmātmā satataṃ dharmacāriṇīm
english: And the righteous one saw his mother Kuntī standing near, bowed like a pupil, she who walked ever in the path of dharma.

sanskrit: sa tam abhyarcya rājānaṃ nāma saṃśrāvya cātmanaḥ niṣīdety abhyanujñāto bṛsyām upaviveśa ha
english: Having honored that king and proclaimed his own name aloud, when bidden "Be seated," he took his place upon a mat of grass.

sanskrit: bhīmasenādayaś caiva pāṇḍavāḥ kauravarṣabham abhivādyopasaṃgṛhya niṣeduḥ pārthivājñayā
english: And Bhīmasena and the other Pāṇḍavas, having saluted the bull of the Kurus and clasped his feet, sat down at the king's command.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛto rājā śuśubhe 'tīva kauravaḥ bibhrad brāhmīṃ śriyaṃ dīptāṃ devair iva bṛhaspatiḥ
english: Surrounded by them, that Kaurava king shone exceedingly, bearing a brahmic splendor blazing forth, like Bṛhaspati amid the gods.

sanskrit: tathā teṣūpaviṣṭeṣu samājagmur maharṣayaḥ śatayūpaprabhṛtayaḥ kurukṣetranivāsinaḥ
english: As they sat thus, the great sages came together—Śatayūpa and the rest, dwellers of Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: vyāsaś ca bhagavān vipro devarṣigaṇapūjitaḥ vṛtaḥ śiṣyair mahātejā darśayām āsa taṃ nṛpam
english: And the lord Vyāsa, the brahmin honored by the host of divine sages, of great splendor, encircled by his disciples, presented himself to that king.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā kauravyaḥ kuntīputraś ca vīryavān bhīmasenādayaś caiva samutthāyābhyapūjayan
english: Then the Kaurava king, and the valiant son of Kuntī, and Bhīmasena and the rest, rose up and paid him honor.

sanskrit: samāgatas tato vyāsaḥ śatayūpādibhir vṛtaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahīpālam āsyatām ity abhāṣata
english: Then Vyāsa, drawing near, encircled by Śatayūpa and the others, said to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the guardian of earth, "Let all be seated."

sanskrit: navaṃ tu viṣṭaraṃ kauśyaṃ kṛṣṇājinakuśottaram pratipede tadā vyāsas tadartham upakalpitam
english: And a fresh seat of kuśa grass, spread over with a black antelope-skin and topped with kuśa, prepared for that very purpose, Vyāsa then took.

sanskrit: te ca sarve dvijaśreṣṭhā viṣṭareṣu samantataḥ dvaipāyanābhyanujñātā niṣedur vipulaujasaḥ
english: And all those best of brahmins, of ample might, by Dvaipāyana's leave, sat down upon seats all around.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā samupaviṣṭeṣu pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu vyāsaḥ satyavatīputraḥ provācāmantrya pārthivam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the great-souled Pāṇḍavas had thus taken their seats, Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, addressed the king and spoke.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra mahābāho kaccit te vardhate tapaḥ kaccin manas te prīṇāti vanavāse narādhipa
english: "Dhṛtarāṣṭra, mighty-armed, does your austerity prosper? Does your mind find contentment in this dwelling in the forest, O lord of men?

sanskrit: kaccid dhṛdi na te śoko rājan putravināśajaḥ kaccij jñānāni sarvāṇi prasannāni tavānagha
english: Is there no grief in your heart, O king, born of the loss of your sons? Are all your faculties of knowledge serene, O blameless one?

sanskrit: kaccid buddhiṃ dṛḍhāṃ kṛtvā carasy āraṇyakaṃ vidhim kaccid vadhūś ca gāndhārī na śokenābhibhūyate
english: Do you, having made your resolve firm, follow the rule of forest life? And is your daughter-in-law Gāndhārī not overcome by sorrow?

sanskrit: mahāprajñā buddhimatī devī dharmārthadarśinī āgamāpāyatattvajñā kaccid eṣā na śocati
english: That queen of great wisdom and understanding, who discerns dharma and artha, who knows the truth of coming and going—does she not grieve?

sanskrit: kaccit kuntī ca rājaṃs tvāṃ śuśrūṣur anahaṃkṛtā yā parityajya rājyaṃ svaṃ guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratā
english: And does Kuntī, O king, serve you free of all pride, she who, forsaking her own kingdom, delights in the service of her elders?

sanskrit: kaccid dharmasuto rājā tvayā prītyābhinanditaḥ bhīmārjunayamāś caiva kaccid ete 'pi sāntvitāḥ
english: Has the king, the son of Dharma, been welcomed by you with affection? And Bhīma, Arjuna, and the twins—have these too been consoled?

sanskrit: kaccin nandasi dṛṣṭvaitān kaccit te nirmalaṃ manaḥ kaccid viśuddhabhāvo 'si jātajñāno narādhipa
english: Do you rejoice to see them? Is your mind unstained? Are you of purified nature, O lord of men, with knowledge now arisen in you?"
